data.exact_reserve_text: During 2023 there has been a deterioration on discontinued business of $7.9m, which was largely offset by improvements on other lines and strong investment income, leading to an overall deterioration of $1.3m for the closed years.
specific_events: Flood and wildfire losses in Greece

prior_year_events.impact_description: Monitored as an ongoing geopolitical situation; directors noted it but did not expect material losses to the Syndicate in the year; reserves monitored and unchanged during the year.
Total expected loss for this event has deteriorated slightly during 2023; gross position increased while recoveries remained broadly unchanged.

named_events.loss_description: Our largest individual loss in 2023 emanated from the Upstream Energy portfolio - a fire broke out at the Nohoch platform, situated in the Cantarell Field, Campeche, Offshore Mexico (known as Pemex).
There was a major earthquake in Turkey and Hurricane Otis in Mexico and our sympathies go to all those impacted by these devastating events.
Other international losses included events in Italy, windstorm Ciaran in France, flood losses in New Zealand, flood and wildfire losses in Greece.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2023 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding were $341.747m (statement currency USD). The report states an overall deterioration on closed years (net) of $1.3m during 2023 and a deterioration on discontinued business of $7.9m. The technical notes show a gross movement in claims outstanding (total change) during 2023 of $25.133m, but that figure includes current year development and is not an explicit gross prioryear movement. Causes cited across the report include adverse claims development, large individual manmade losses (notably an Upstream Energy fire at the Nohoch platform), natural catastrophe losses (e.g. Hurricane Otis, windstorm events) and inflation/claims cost pressures. The syndicate notes ongoing monitoring of geopolitical exposures (Ukraine/Russia) and pandemic related impacts.
raw_causal_phrases: During 2023 there has been a deterioration on discontinued business of $7.9m, which was largely offset by improvements on other lines and strong investment income, leading to an overall deterioration of $1.3m for the closed years.
Our largest individual loss in 2023 emanated from the Upstream Energy portfolio - a fire broke out at the Nohoch platform, situated in the Cantarell Field, Campeche, Offshore Mexico (known as Pemex).
The Space market also had poor experience during 2023 often attaching to 2022 policies.

Other international losses included events in Italy, windstorm Ciaran in France, flood losses in New Zealand, flood and wildfire losses in Greece. There was a major earthquake in Turkey and Hurricane Otis in Mexico and our sympathies go to all those impacted by these devastating events.
Inflation remained a key topic of focus in 2023.
The Property Reinsurance market saw a structural reset in terms and conditions, attachment level and pricing during 2023.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Technical provisions table (Claims outstanding balance at 1 January). The report does not present an explicit aggregate GROSS 'movement in prior year's provision' figure; narrative provides net closed years deterioration ($1.3m) and discontinued business deterioration ($7.9m). The technical reconciliation table shows a gross 'Change in claims outstanding' of $25.133m but that includes current-year movements and is not a pure prior-year movement. A gross prioryear development figure could not be unambiguously extracted. There is potential distortion from SPA/RITC activity referenced in the report which can affect development tables.
